title: Gideon and the Crown
premise: Tamsin Quintana, the last swordspeaker sworn to a dead god, smuggles relics through the Thornfell mountains while pretending the old covenant is merely broken, not murdered. When prayers begin landing again — answered by something wearing the old gods' voices — Tamsin discovers the crown of Thornfell was forged from a stolen divine name, and the royal line has been feeding on it for two centuries. Guided by Ilse Vane, a priestess who remembers a past life she shouldn't, and hunted by his former oath-brother Ser Roderic, Tamsin must carry the true name back to the gods' mountain before the coronation of a child-king seals the theft forever. He succeeds only by surrendering his own memories of Ilse as the price of the reforged covenant — and the book ends with her choosing to teach him to love her again, one remembered story at a time.
about_author: August Winterbourne is the pen name of a former mountain guide who claims to have mapped every pass in a range that does not appear on any official survey. They write fantasy from a cabin with unreliable electricity and a firm rule that every oath in a story must cost something.

chapters.title: The Toll of Small Prayers
chapters.summary: Tamsin Quintana guides a relic shipment through the Thornfell passes, trading wry banter with his mule-driver crew. A shrine that has been silent for two centuries answers a dying boy's prayer, and the mountain goes still. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — the world he trusts has just blinked.

chapters.title: A Woman with Someone Else's Memories
chapters.summary: In the border town of Lowmark, priestess Ilse Vane recognizes Tamsin on sight and greets him by a name he never gave her — a name from a life she lived before her own. She insists the gods are waking and that he is the key. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: disoriented attraction, the first crack in his cynicism.

chapters.title: What the Crown Is Made Of
chapters.summary: Ilse shows Tamsin a stolen royal ledger: the Thornfell crown contains a bound divine name, siphoned at the last coronation, which is why prayers died. The child-king's crowning will consume the last fragment. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose — the theft is almost complete.

chapters.title: The Oath-Brother's Warrant
chapters.summary: Ser Roderic, Tamsin's oath-brother from the dead swordspeaker order, arrives with a royal warrant and an offer: betray the priestess, be restored to his name and lands. Their duel of words ends in a draw and a warning. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship already half-buried.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: Fleeing Lowmark, Tamsin leads Ilse and her small fellowship through the Hollow Steps, a pass that exists on no map. He tests her claims by asking the mountain for a sign — and the mountain answers him personally. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder; the god he swore to might not be dead.

chapters.title: The Choir Under the Ice
chapters.summary: In a frozen cave chapel, the fellowship finds the swordspeakers' lost reliquary, and Tamsin hears the voices of every oath-brother who died believing he abandoned them. Ilse anchors him through the vision. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: guilt surfaced and shared — intimacy born in a haunted place.

chapters.title: A King Who Is Only Nine
chapters.summary: The fellowship reaches the capital in disguise during coronation festivities. Tamsin glimpses the child-king Aldric and realizes the boy is a vessel being hollowed, not a villain. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: moral complication — the enemy is a frightened child.

chapters.title: Roderic's Version of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Roderic corners Tamsin in a tavern and tells his own truth: the order died because Tamsin's master refused to serve the crown, and loyalty to the realm is all Roderic has left. He lets Tamsin go — this once. POV: Roderic. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist; loyalty as a wound.

chapters.title: The Name in the Vault
chapters.summary: Ilse's past-life memory leads them beneath the palace to the crown vault, where the stolen divine name whispers in her voice. Tamsin realizes the god has been wearing Ilse's first life as a mask. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo — her identity is not entirely her own.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: One of the fellowship sells their route to the crown to buy his family's freedom. The escape through the Salt Gate costs two lives, and Tamsin carries a wounded Ilse into the high country. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: rage and grief; the cost of trust made flesh.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Asks
chapters.summary: Healing in a shepherd's bothy, Tamsin and Ilse finally speak plainly of love and of the vision that showed him her past life. The god's voice comes to him in a dream with a price: a memory of his choosing, to balance the name's return. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by a bargain neither names aloud.

chapters.title: The Regent's Hunt
chapters.summary: The Regent Veyra declares the priestess a heretic and floods the passes with soldiers. Roderic, ordered to kill rather than capture, begins quietly sabotaging the hunt from within. POV: Roderic. Emotional beat: a loyal man discovering his loyalty serves a lie.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Old Promises
chapters.summary: The fellowship must cross a rope bridge the swordspeakers once swore to guard. Tamsin speaks his first true swordspeaking in fifteen years and the bridge remembers him. Half the fellowship crosses before Veyra's vanguard arrives. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: exultation and terror — the old power is real and hungry.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Reliquary
chapters.summary: Veyra burns the cave chapel and the reliquary to deny the gods their footholds. Tamsin watches two centuries of his order's memory go up in smoke and swears, finally and completely, to finish the covenant. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: loss transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Roderic Breaks His Oath
chapters.summary: Roderic refuses a direct order to execute captured villagers, turns his sword on his own company, and barely escapes to bring Tamsin the coronation date and Veyra's plan to crown the boy early. POV: Roderic. Emotional beat: redemption bought at the price of everything he was.

chapters.title: The Ascent to the Gods' Mountain
chapters.summary: The final climb through storm to the summit shrine where the covenant was first sworn. Ilse's borrowed memories begin unraveling — the god is reclaiming its mask — and she starts forgetting which life is hers. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: race against erasure, love sharpened by approaching loss.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: At the summit, Tamsin speaks the divine name back to the sky. The god demands its balance: not Ilse's life, but a memory of Tamsin's choosing. He offers every memory of Ilse — their whole brief history — and the covenant seals. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: sacrifice at its most intimate; duty devouring love by his own hand.

chapters.title: Coronation Interrupted
chapters.summary: The reforged covenant shatters the crown's stolen power mid-coronation. The boy-king Aldric, suddenly his own person, names Veyra's theft before the assembled realm. Roderic arrests her; the old gods' quiet presence settles over Thornfell like snow. POV: Roderic. Emotional beat: catharsis — the machinery of theft exposed and stopped.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Face
chapters.summary: Tamsin wakes on the mountainside with no memory of Ilse at all. She finds him there, and he greets her politely, the way one greets a stranger. She carries their whole history alone. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: heartbreak held with dignity; love without recognition.

chapters.title: The New Covenant's First Winter
chapters.summary: Months later, shrines across Thornfell answer prayers honestly, and Tamsin has become the reluctant teacher of a new swordspeaker order. Ilse serves at the rebuilt chapel in Lowmark. They orbit each other, courteous and aching. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: quiet melancholy — a life rebuilt around a missing room.

chapters.title: Stories as an Act of Defiance
chapters.summary: Ilse begins telling Tamsin one story of them each week, refusing to let their history die just because he can't hold it. He starts to feel the shape of what he lost — a laugh he misses, a fear he can't place. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: patient, stubborn hope; memory kept alive by retelling.

chapters.title: The First Word of a New Oath
chapters.summary: On the anniversary of the reforging, Tamsin asks Ilse to tell him the story of the bridge — and instead of grief, he feels recognition. He asks her to tell him another tomorrow, and the one after that. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: resolution not as restoration but as choice — love beginning again, on purpose.
